subject: landscape confusion
comment: Dear Mr. Wharton, I am writing to express my deep disappointment regarding the recent amendments to the City's Landscaping and Buffers rules. As a resident who has diligently followed the guidelines set forth by the Utah Water Savers and participated in the Landscaping Conversion Incentive Program, I find it incredibly disheartening to learn that the very expensive landscaping project we undertook, which was previously approved under the program, may now require additional expenditures to comply with the new regulations. Our project, which aimed to conserve water and contribute to the sustainability efforts of our community, was meticulously planned and executed, with considerable financial investment on our part. However, the recent amendments seem to disregard these efforts and impose further financial burdens on residents who have already contributed to water conservation initiatives. What perplexes me even more is the apparent disparity in priorities reflected by these amendments. While we are being penalized for our proactive measures to conserve water, our neighbor continues to waste water by watering his grass twice a day, resulting in continuous runoff. Such inconsistencies in enforcement not only undermine the integrity of the regulations but also fail to address the urgent issue of water scarcity, particularly in the face of the ongoing drought in Utah. It is deeply concerning that the City Council's decision appears to be out of touch with the current environmental challenges we are facing. Instead of incentivizing and supporting residents who invest in sustainable practices, these amendments seem regressive and punitive. I urge the City Council to reconsider the recent amendments to the Landscaping and Buffers rules and to prioritize policies that encourage and reward water conservation efforts. It is crucial that we work together as a community to address the pressing issue of water scarcity and ensure the long-term sustainability of our city. Thank you for considering my concerns. I look forward to seeing positive changes that reflect the best interests of our community and the environment. Sincerely, Alissa Kean

subject: From a Fellow Westminster Alum
